questions.q: What does a hypervisor actually do?
options: It abstracts a physical machine's CPU, memory, storage, and network into virtual resources that multiple VMs can use
It replaces the need for physical servers entirely
It only manages network cabling between servers
It is a type of physical hard drive used in datacenters
questions.explain: A hypervisor carves fixed physical resources into virtual CPU, memory, storage, and network resources, each handed to a separate VM.

questions.q: What distinguishes a Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisor from a Type 2 (hosted) hypervisor?
options: Type 1 installs directly on the hardware with no host OS underneath; Type 2 installs as an application on top of a host OS
Type 1 only runs on laptops; Type 2 only runs in datacenters
There is no real difference — the terms are interchangeable
Type 2 hypervisors don't support virtual machines at all
questions.explain: Type 1 hypervisors like ESXi, Hyper-V, and KVM run directly on hardware. Type 2 hypervisors like VirtualBox run as an application on top of a regular OS.

questions.q: Which of these is a real example of a Type 2 (hosted) hypervisor?
options: VMware ESXi
Microsoft Hyper-V (Server role)
KVM
Oracle VirtualBox
questions.explain: VirtualBox installs as an application on top of an existing OS, making it a hosted, Type 2 hypervisor. ESXi, Hyper-V, and KVM are all Type 1.

questions.q: Why do production datacenters and public cloud providers almost always run Type 1 hypervisors on their physical servers?
options: Type 1 hypervisors are free while Type 2 hypervisors require a paid license
There is no host OS competing for CPU, memory, and I/O, so performance is near-native
Type 2 hypervisors cannot run more than one VM at a time
Type 1 hypervisors do not require any physical hardware
questions.explain: Without a general-purpose host OS competing for resources, a Type 1 hypervisor delivers near-native performance, which is why it's standard in production.

questions.q: In the Type 1 stack 'Hardware -> Hypervisor -> VM1 / VM2 / VM3', what sits directly on top of the hypervisor?
options: A host operating system
The physical network switch
The virtual machines themselves
A second hypervisor
questions.explain: In a Type 1 (bare-metal) stack, the hypervisor runs directly on hardware and the VMs sit directly on top of it — no host OS layer in between.
